newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended a low-volume trading day fractionally firmer on Friday, paring midday gains in a late session pursuit of seesawing bunds.

Dealers said that after the release of bond-friendly U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) and jobs data the afternoon session was spent chasing the bund contract which spiked at 100.1 before retreating.
"There was no massive turnover, though," a dealer said.
The 10-year January benchmark strongly outperformed the April 2006 bund, widening the discount to 15 basis points late in the session from 13 earlier.
Prior to the U.S. numbers trade was low-key, with most activity generated by position squaring.
Dealers said earlier the pressure on the short end of recent days caused by money market tightness on the back of a high-priced Dutch Treasury Certificate programme was easing.
Support for the short end came from Friday's extra liquidity allocation to the money market by the Dutch central bank, leading to some bid activity in 1998 and 1999 paper.
However, the 6.25 pct July 1998 ended the day at 104.16/24, down from Thursday's 104.22/30.
